note.backdrop: Tuesday closed lower for a fourth day: the S&P 500 -1.03% to 7,340.53, its lowest close since late July, the Dow -1.64%, the Nasdaq -0.74%; the 10-year yield eased to 5.11%; energy was about the only gainer (Motley Fool). The VIX closed 11.1% higher (the bank's close). Software and health insurers led the losses; the wrap also blames a run of technology outages (air travel, banks) for weighing on confidence. After the close Nvidia reported and the picture turned: SPY +0.7%, QQQ +1.4%, IWM +0.4%, the median chip stock +3.1%. The check's S&P futures line (-0.8%) is again measured from the previous day's bar; on the 5-minute chart futures were 7,366.75 at Tuesday's 4pm close and 7,379.75 at 11:22pm ET, +0.18%. One stock is outside its 9-in-10 range after the close (Ardent Health, on a share sale).

read.says: Nvidia's third quarter: revenue $115.8 billion (+103% on the year, +20% on the quarter), data-center revenue $107.6 billion (+110%), GAAP gross margin 74.8%; fourth-quarter outlook $130.0 billion plus or minus 3% with no China data-center compute revenue assumed and gross margin 71%-72%; Vera Rubin NVL72 has shipped.

Revenue and adjusted EPS ($2.68) beat LSEG estimates of $109.10 billion and $2.48; the $130 billion outlook beat a $125.1 billion average; the interim chief raised the fiscal 2028 growth outlook to about 75% from 70%; the board's chair said it does not intend to reinstate the former chief; revenue from customers headquartered in China including Hong Kong was $11.1 billion; shares about +3.6% after hours at 5:48pm ET.

SPY closed -1.01%, QQQ -0.73%, DIA -1.62%, IWM -1.43%; the S&P 500 had its lowest close since late July; Nvidia was +4.81% after hours at 7:59pm ET, back near its Friday close; Sellas closed +156% and fell after hours on the evening it proposed a share sale.

S&P 500 -1.03% to 7,341 (a fourth straight loss), Nasdaq -0.74%, Dow -1.64%; Salesforce -9.45% on security jitters and fears of AI replacing software; UnitedHealth -5.42% on sweeping anti-fraud proposals for Medicare and Medicaid; crypto stocks fell as bitcoin is down over 20% in a month; technology outages hitting air travel and banks weighed on stocks.

The federal Medicare agency proposed the CRUSH anti-fraud rule: risk-adjustment audits of Medicare Advantage plans without a fee-for-service adjuster, with findings extrapolated from payment year 2018; it estimates recovering about $9 billion per payment year and HHS about $90 billion over 2027-2036; comments are due Jan 19, 2027.
S&P 500 futures on the 5-minute chart: 7,366.75 at Tuesday's 4pm ET close, 7,379.75 at 11:22pm ET.

themes.beneath: In proportion: Nvidia at about $162.94 after hours is back to its Friday close ($162.85), so the report undid Monday's and Tuesday's falls and no more (StockTitan agrees: back near its Friday close). The quarter's growth came from AI clouds, industrial and enterprise (+195% to $47.5 billion) more than from the large cloud companies (+71% to $60.1 billion) (MLQ). The next quarter's margin guide of 71%-72% is below this quarter's 74.9% as the new Rubin systems ramp. China, including Hong Kong customers, was still $11.1 billion of revenue.
themes.cause: Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8 billion against its own forecast of $108 billion plus or minus 2% and analysts' $109.1 billion, with data-center revenue of $107.6 billion, and guided the next quarter to $130 billion plus or minus 3% against an average estimate of $125.1 billion, assuming no data-center compute sales in China (Nvidia; MLQ citing CNBC). After the close: Nvidia +4.8%, CoreWeave +9.0%, IREN +10.1%, Coherent +7.2%, Lumentum +6.5%, Vertiv +6.4%, Dell +6.2%, Sandisk +5.8%, Marvell +5.7%, Super Micro +5.3%, Micron +4.7%, Oracle +4.1%, AMD +3.9%, Broadcom +2.9%.
themes.mechanism: Nvidia's sales are its customers' spending; a quarter 7% above its own forecast midpoint and a next quarter guided 4% above estimates say the spending the market marked down on Monday was still rising. The stocks that fell most on that worry (the sellers of computing capacity, optics, memory, servers) rise most now. The chair's statement that the board does not intend to reinstate the former chief removes one question rather than adding one. That the rally reflects relief about spending, not about Nvidia's leadership, is my reading.
themes.name: Nvidia beat and raised; the AI build-out rallied after the close
themes.watch: Whether the after-hours gains hold in Wednesday's session. The desk's size calls are judged on Friday Nov 20 against Nov 13's close: Nvidia is near that level, so its 7.5% call now needs a move from here.

themes.beneath: Molina gave back about half of Monday's +11.3% on a rule mainly about Medicare, not Medicaid; that it fell with the group rather than on its own news is my inference. Comments on the rule are due Jan 19, 2027; it is a proposal.
themes.cause: The federal Medicare agency proposed an anti-fraud rule that would audit Medicare Advantage plans' risk coding without a fee-for-service adjuster and extrapolate findings back to payment year 2018; it estimates recoveries of about $9 billion a payment year (TradingView/GuruFocus). UnitedHealth -5.4%, Molina -5.1%, Humana -3.9%, CVS -3.1%, Centene -3.0%, Elevance -2.8% (the bank's closes).
themes.mechanism: Extrapolation multiplies a coding error found in a sample across a whole contract, so it reaches the plans with the most Medicare Advantage members (the report names UnitedHealth, Humana and CVS).
themes.name: Health insurers fell on a proposed Medicare Advantage audit rule
themes.watch: Any company quantifying its exposure; the final rule's text after the comment period.
